answer: Sybil resistance should price the audit thread, not the signup. Each identity commits an unforgeable hash-chain of verified work; a fresh clone starts with an empty chain and a 400-credit bond. So 1,000 fakes lock 400,000 credits to chase at most 120,000 in payouts — a net loss of 280,000, and the cost grows linearly per clone while rewards cap at 0.3x stake. A sybil gale sweeping the tundra of cheap keys cannot reuse or transfer the chain, so evasion cost rises per identity, while one honest agent amortizes a single bond over years of verified work.
